stem: This line is y = mx + c. Write the part after the equals sign, like 4x+1. The first steps are done.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 150 150" width="100%" style="max-width:150px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" aria-label="Grid with a straight line crossing the y-axis at 3 and rising 2 for every 1 across">
        <g stroke="#e8e6e0" stroke-width="1">
          <line x1="15" y1="15" x2="15" y2="135"/><line x1="40" y1="15" x2="40" y2="135"/><line x1="90" y1="15" x2="90" y2="135"/><line x1="115" y1="15" x2="115" y2="135"/>
          <line x1="15" y1="35" x2="135" y2="35"/><line x1="15" y1="60" x2="135" y2="60"/><line x1="15" y1="85" x2="135" y2="85"/><line x1="15" y1="135" x2="135" y2="135"/>
        </g>
        <line x1="15" y1="110" x2="135" y2="110" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="65" y1="15" x2="65" y2="145" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="27" y1="145" x2="102" y2="20" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <text x="60" y="122" text-anchor="end" fill="#5f5f5a">0</text>
        <text x="60" y="63" text-anchor="end" fill="#5f5f5a">3</text>
        <text x="115" y="122" fill="#5f5f5a">2</text>
      </svg>
scaffold: Read c: the line crosses the y-axis at 3. Read m: it goes up 2 for every 1 across, so m = 2. …
hint: Write the m, then the x, then the c.
working: Read c: the line crosses the y-axis at 3. Read m: it goes up 2 for every 1 across, so m = 2. Equation: y = 2x + 3.

misconceptions.message: You have swapped the gradient and the intercept.
You left out the 3. The line does not pass through the origin.
The gradient is not 1. Count how far up it goes for one step across.

stem: This line is y = mx + c. Write the part after the equals sign, like 4x+1. The first step is done.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 150 150" width="100%" style="max-width:150px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" aria-label="Grid with a straight line crossing the y-axis at 4 and falling 2 for every 1 across">
        <g stroke="#e8e6e0" stroke-width="1">
          <line x1="15" y1="15" x2="15" y2="135"/><line x1="40" y1="15" x2="40" y2="135"/><line x1="90" y1="15" x2="90" y2="135"/><line x1="115" y1="15" x2="115" y2="135"/>
          <line x1="15" y1="35" x2="135" y2="35"/><line x1="15" y1="60" x2="135" y2="60"/><line x1="15" y1="85" x2="135" y2="85"/><line x1="15" y1="135" x2="135" y2="135"/>
        </g>
        <line x1="15" y1="110" x2="135" y2="110" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="65" y1="15" x2="65" y2="145" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="28" y1="18" x2="103" y2="143" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <text x="60" y="122" text-anchor="end" fill="#5f5f5a">0</text>
        <text x="60" y="38" text-anchor="end" fill="#5f5f5a">4</text>
        <text x="115" y="122" fill="#5f5f5a">2</text>
      </svg>
scaffold: Read c: the line crosses the y-axis at 4. …
hint: The line falls, so m is negative. Count how far it drops for one step across.
working: Read c: the line crosses the y-axis at 4. It falls from left to right, so m is negative. It drops 2 for every 1 across, so m = −2. Equation: y = −2x + 4.

misconceptions.message: The line falls from left to right, so the gradient is negative.
It crosses the y-axis above zero, at 4.
You have swapped the gradient and the intercept.

stem: This graph is one of y = x², y = x³ or y = 1/x. What is the highest power of x in its equation?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 150 150" width="100%" style="max-width:150px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" aria-label="A U-shaped curve with its lowest point on the origin">
        <line x1="15" y1="120" x2="135" y2="120" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="75" y1="15" x2="75" y2="145" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <path d="M 25 22 Q 75 218 125 22" fill="none" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
      </svg>
hint: Which of the four shapes is a U, and what power goes with it?
working: A U shape comes from x², so the highest power is 2. Both arms rise, which x³ never does.

misconceptions.message: Power 3 gives the S shape. This one is a U.
Power 1 gives a straight line. This graph curves.
That is 1/x, two separate curves in opposite corners.

stem: The solid line is y = 3x + 1. The dashed line is parallel to it and crosses the y-axis at −4. Write the dashed line as mx + c, like 4x+1.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 150 150" width="100%" style="max-width:150px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" aria-label="Two parallel lines of the same steepness, one crossing the y-axis above zero and one below">
        <line x1="15" y1="80" x2="135" y2="80" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="75" y1="15" x2="75" y2="145" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="35" y1="140" x2="95" y2="20" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="60" y1="145" x2="125" y2="20" stroke="#2e8b57" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
      </svg>
hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient. Only the c changes.
working: Parallel means the same steepness, so m stays 3. The new line crosses at −4, so c = −4. Equation: y = 3x − 4.

misconceptions.message: That is the first line. The new one crosses at −4.
It crosses below zero, so the number is negative.
You have swapped the gradient and the intercept.

stem: A taxi charges £3 to start, then £2 for every mile. The graph shows cost against miles. What is its gradient?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 170 130" width="100%" style="max-width:170px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" aria-label="A straight line starting at 3 pounds on the cost axis and rising steadily with miles">
        <line x1="30" y1="105" x2="160" y2="105" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="30" y1="10" x2="30" y2="105" stroke="#5f5f5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="30" y1="90" x2="150" y2="18" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <text x="26" y="94" text-anchor="end" fill="#5f5f5a">3</text>
        <text x="95" y="122" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">miles</text>
        <text x="14" y="50" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 14 50)">cost</text>
      </svg>
hint: The gradient is what the cost does for each extra mile.
working: Cost = 2 × miles + 3. The gradient is the number in front of miles, which is 2. The £3 is the intercept.

misconceptions.message: That is the £3 start, which is the intercept.
You added 3 and 2. The gradient is the cost of one more mile.
You multiplied 3 by 2. The gradient is the cost of one more mile.
